title: Scheduling and Consistency
summary: Consistency is more effective than bursts — Use batching and a content calendar with three posts each week.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **Consistency wins** **over bursts**. **Success in content** **comes not from posting once with great impact** — **but from having a steady rhythm** **that people can rely on**.
- **Three regular posts each week** **are stronger than a week of intense posting** **followed by two weeks of silence**.
bullets: **What will you understand?** **Consistency wins** **over bursts**. **Success in content** **comes not from posting once with great impact** — **but from having a steady rhythm** **that people can rely on**.
**Three regular posts each week** **are stronger than a week of intense posting** **followed by two weeks of silence**.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Temporary excitement** **breaks your plan**.
- **Most disruptions start from a daily exhausting question:** “**What should I post today?**” **When it repeats every day** — **the decision itself becomes a burden**.
- **Without a clear schedule** — **even good content comes out sporadically** **and the audience doesn’t know when to expect you**.
bullets: **Most disruptions start from a daily exhausting question:** “**What should I post today?**” **When it repeats every day** — **the decision itself becomes a burden**.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: A Simple System: Batch + Calendar
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Set a fixed weekly slot** **for shooting or preparing in batches** — **Batching** **solves the time issue** **instead of putting out daily fires**.
- **After preparation** — **set specific publishing dates:** **three times a week, for example**. **A clear content calendar**.
- **The rule:** **consistency beats bursts**. **Be sustainable** **before being perfect**. **Maintain a steady cadence**.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Random Cadence or Steady Cadence?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Without a System | With a Clear System |
|-----------|------------|
| **Post when you feel like it** — **a week of 5 posts and a week of nothing** — **stress and decreased engagement** | **Fixed preparation day + 3 fixed posting days** — **less effort and higher audience expectations** |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Execution Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **Batching** | **Group the same type of work** **at once** | **Shoot 3 videos** **in one session** |
| **Content Calendar** | **A schedule with publishing dates** **and types of content in advance** | **Monday Tip** — **Wednesday Story** — **Friday Light CTA** |
| **Cadence** | **The steady rhythm** **you follow in posting** | **3 posts a week** **for 8 consecutive weeks** |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Check
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** **Your goal is consistency** **and you have 4 hours available each week** — **which plan is closest to long-term success?**

Post daily** **when I feel like it.
**I will create 3 posts each week** **with a fixed schedule + slot batching**.
I will wait a whole week** **until I prepare 10 perfect posts.

**Explanation:** **A fixed, actionable plan** **is better than large, hard-to-commit plans** — **this is the essence of consistency**.
